description: The exact CPV code set for Hungarian banking/payments procurement was not empirically validated against live notices (only 66110000 banking services was confirmed conceptually).

Special-sector (közszolgáltatói / utilities) contracting entities — energy, water, transport operators — procure banking and card-acceptance services under a distinct Kbt. regime; this pass did not separately map their notice practices beyond one incidental example (BKV).

Hungarian central-government institutions largely bank through the Magyar Államkincstár (State Treasury) rather than tendering commercial accounts; this exemption boundary was not verified in this pass.
Annual közbeszerzési terv (procurement plan) publications — which precede notices by months — were identified only generically via buyer-side pages, not as a systematically collectable set.
EKR and the Közbeszerzési Értesítő publish almost exclusively in Hungarian; only TED provides English versions, and only for above-threshold notices.
Purchases made under KEF and DKÜ framework agreements (call-offs) may not generate individual EKR notices, making a material share of state payments/IT spend invisible to notice-only monitoring.

The TED Search API was documented but not actually exercised with a HUN + banking-CPV expert query in this pass, so the real volume, notice-type mix and CPV distribution of Hungarian banking/payments notices is unmeasured.

No verified mapping was established between Hungarian national notice identifiers (Közbeszerzési Értesítő / EKR numbers) and TED notice IDs, which is required to deduplicate the EU-level duplicates against the national layer covered by other cells.

Banking/payments procurement frequently hides under IT and consulting CPVs (72000000 IT services, 48000000 software, 79000000 business services) rather than 66xxxxxx, e.g. core-banking, card personalisation, ATM/POS estate and cash-logistics contracts.
Opentender.eu's Hungarian data freshness is unknown; DIGIWHIST funding ended in 2018 and the dataset may be stale for recent years.
EU-level financing bodies that fund Hungarian financial-sector projects outside cohesion policy — EIB, EIF, EBRD project registers and their tender pages — were not covered in this pass.

Hungarian-language searching was performed for programme, RRF and financial-instrument terms, but not for TED-specific Hungarian notice vocabulary as it appears inside eForms HU-language notices (e.g. 'ajánlati felhívás', 'tájékoztató az eljárás eredményéről', 'keretmegállapodás').

Prosecution-side and criminal-law sources (Legfőbb Ügyészség / ügyészség.hu, Nemzeti Adó- és Vámhivatal bid-rigging investigations, KEHI successor bodies) were not searched in this pass, though bid-rigging in tenders (versenyt korlátozó megállapodás közbeszerzési eljárásban, Btk. 420. §) is a distinct disclosure channel.

No sector-specific pass on the actual banking/payments contracting authorities and their disputes — e.g. Magyar Államkincstár, MNB, Közbeszerzési és Ellátási Főigazgatóság (KEF), NISZ, GIRO/Takarékbank/OTP/K&H as bidders — nor on their appearance as parties in KDB cases.

English-language coverage of this cell is thin: KDB decisions, ÁSZ audits and GVH decisions are published primarily in Hungarian, with only selective English summaries (asz.hu/en, gvh.hu English pages).
No confirmed machine-readable feed (API, RSS, open-data dump) was identified for KDB decisions, KH decision database, or ÁSZ reports.
Historical depth of the online KDB decision archive (how far back decisions are published, and whether pre-2015 Kbt. era cases remain accessible) was not established.
No aggregator in this cell provides banking/payments-specific curation for Hungary, so sector relevance must be derived by us from CPV codes and buyer identities applied across horizontal feeds.

The cell's core rationale is that aggregators surface below-threshold (nemzeti értékhatár alatti) calls invisible in TED. Two sources plausibly deliver this - Tender-Értesítő/khf.hu commercially and Opentender.eu openly - but neither was recall-tested, and the rest are likely TED-derived.
Commercial bank and payment-processor procurement in Hungary is essentially unserved by tender aggregators; only bolt-on 'magán beszerzés' claims exist and they are unvalidated.

This pass did not specifically probe for aggregators focused on Hungarian utility-sector (közszolgáltató) or state-owned-enterprise buyers, which procure payment and cash-handling systems under a separate utilities regime.

No robots.txt, terms-of-service, or API licensing document was reviewed for any candidate. Collection-method suggestions are therefore provisional, and 'collection_allowed' reflects general plausibility rather than a legal review.

The khf.hu to tender-ertesito.hu redirect suggests consolidation, but corporate ownership across the Hungarian aggregator brands (Tender Service Group, TenderMonitor, Napitender, KözbeszGuru, InnoTender) was not mapped.

Only two examples of the local/regional press layer (Civishír for Debrecen, kisvarda.hu municipal site) were reached. Hungary has ~19 county-level media ecosystems (largely consolidated county dailies plus independent local sites) that report municipal account-holder tenders.
No archive or historical backfill route was established for the trade titles (Computerworld pre-2024 issues, older Bitport/HWSW content) which is where multi-year vendor-award patterns live.

Paywalled/print-only trade content (HVG print, Figyelő-type weeklies, ComputerTrends print magazine, BBJ magazine) was not assessed for access route; these often carry the CIO interviews naming systems and integrators.
English-language coverage of Hungarian banking deals was found to be thin — BBJ and Portfolio's English edition are the realistic options; no English outlet covers Hungarian procurement in depth.

The bank-side actor map is only partially built (OTP, MBH, K&H, CIB, Erste, Raiffeisen, Gránit, UniCredit, Magyar Bankholding legacy brands, MNB, Magyar Államkincstár) and the vendor/integrator side is barely mapped for Hungary.

The core member/sponsor rosters (bankszovetseg.hu/tagjaink detail pages, hunfintech.com/membership, ivsz.hu/tagok, amcham.hu directory, ahkungarn.hu member search, Portfolio /tamogatok tabs) were identified but their full contents were not enumerated in this scouting pass.

Bilateral chambers beyond AmCham and DUIHK (British, French, Italian, Nordic, Swiss, Austrian chambers in Hungary) were not searched, and neither were sector bodies such as the Hungarian e-commerce association, the insurance association (MABISZ) or the securities/market infrastructure bodies around BÉT/KELER.
Sponsor rosters are only useful as a time series, but historic event pages (pre-2017 Portfolio events, archived IIR Joomla pages, discontinued conferences) were not systematically enumerated.
English-language coverage of this cell is thin: only AmCham and an event aggregator were found in English. Hungarian associations mostly publish rosters in Hungarian only.
No method has yet been defined for joining association/sponsor company names to procurement award-notice supplier records, which is the whole point of this cell for workstream A2.

Career pages were located for MKB/MBH, GIRO and MNB only. Missing first-party career/newsroom feeds for OTP, K&H (KBC), Erste Hungary, Raiffeisen Hungary, UniCredit Hungary, Gránit Bank, Magyar Fejlesztési Bank (MFB), and Magyar Posta / Postai pénzügyi szolgáltatások.

Vendor-side newsrooms and Hungarian career pages were only sampled (Dorsum, Mindspire). Not covered: Intellect/iGCB, Temenos, Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, Euronet, Worldline/SIX, ACI, IND/Backbase-type digital vendors, and Hungarian integrators (4iG, T-Systems Hungary, IBM/Accenture/Deloitte Budapest delivery centres).

No staffing/body-leasing agencies specialising in Hungarian banking IT contractors were identified, although agency-posted contractor ads are the classic tell of a delivery ramp-up under an unannounced contract.
No repeatable method yet for extracting IT/intangible capex lines and named technology partners from Hungarian annual reports at scale.
English-language coverage of Hungarian vendor hiring (international vendors posting Budapest roles in English on their own ATS - Workday, SmartRecruiters, Greenhouse) was not enumerated.

CIB Bank (Intesa Sanpaolo, Italy) and MBH/other foreign-linked entities were not covered; the cell brief named Erste/UniCredit/Raiffeisen/KBC but Intesa is an equally significant Italian parent for Hungary.
Group annual reports and Pillar 3 / sustainability reports of Erste Group, RBI, UniCredit and KBC were not yet mined for supplier-spend, outsourcing and intra-group service disclosures.
TED / OJEU was not directly queried in this pass, although EIB rules require promoter notices to be published there; utilities-sector notices from bank-adjacent entities may also appear.

Bank-level 'üzletszabályzat' / kiszervezett tevékenységek lists — legally required to name outsourced activities and their performers — were identified as a mechanism but not harvested per institution.
Dutch-language coverage for the KBC/K&H leg was only shallow (one query), and German coverage focused on Erste rather than RBI's Austrian supplier channels.
Magyar Államkincstár's statutory közbeszerzés / közérdekű adatok page URL is unresolved.

It is unverified which of GIRO Zrt., KELER Zrt., KELER KSZF Zrt. and MNB fall under the classic vs utility (közszolgáltatói) procurement regime, which determines thresholds and whether notices appear publicly at all.
IT spend of several cell entities is likely executed via DKÜ framework agreements rather than own-name tenders, so a buyer-name-only feed will systematically under-count.
Contracts under national thresholds ('egyéb beszerzés') do not reach EKR/KBA/TED and appear, if at all, only on the buyer's own site or in its 5 MFt+ contract register.
Almost all buyer-side procurement content in this cell is Hungarian-only; the English surfaces found (EXIM /exim-en, TED EN) are partial or lag the Hungarian originals.
Adjacent state-influenced financial buyers (OBA, Szanálási Alap, NAV payment functions, Nemzeti Vagyonkezelő, state-owned MBH/Gránit distribution partners named in MFB tenders) were not scouted.
Award history older than the current site generation sits on legacy archives (mnb.hu/archivum, old kozbeszerzes.hu ertesito paths from 2006 onward) with different URL schemes.
Hospital and hospital-maintainer buyers (OKFŐ / Országos Kórházi Főigazgatóság and individual kórházak) were not mapped to concrete procurement disclosure URLs in this run.
Only Budapest-centred buyers (BKK, BKV, Fővárosi Vízművek, Semmelweis) were concretely identified; county seats and regional Volán/water/waste operators are unmapped.
Purchases below Kbt. thresholds (small municipalities, single POS terminals, small e-payment integrations) are structurally invisible in gazette/TED.
CPV/keyword taxonomy for this cell has not been validated against real notice text (e.g. whether 'számlavezetés' notices use 66110000, 66600000 or services-other codes).
English-language coverage of this cell is thin by nature: only TED carries EN text; municipal, hospital and utility disclosures are Hungarian-only.
No procurement or vendor-facing source located for GRÁNIT Bank, and none for MBH Bank beyond its code of ethics.

Group-level procurement arms of the foreign parents (KBC for K&H, RBI for Raiffeisen, Intesa Sanpaolo for CIB, UniCredit Group Global Sourcing) were only partially reached; searches returned other Raiffeisen network countries (Ukraine, Czechia) rather than Hungary-relevant portals.
Only hu and en were used in this cell, but four of the nine banks are subsidiaries of German/Italian/Dutch-language parents whose procurement documentation is published in those languages.
Vendor-side evidence (press releases, case studies and reference lists published by IT/payments suppliers naming Hungarian banks as customers) was only touched once and yielded little in this pass.
Supplier codes of conduct were confirmed to exist for OTP, Erste, CIB and K&H, but the exact PDF URLs for the OTP Partner Etikai Kódex and the Erste supplier code were not captured in this pass.
The two identified e-sourcing platforms carrying real RFx traffic (SAP Ariba for OTP, Erste Group Procurements for Erste) are invitation- or account-gated.
Fraud/AML and open-banking vendor announcements touching Hungarian banks (e.g. NICE Actimize, BioCatch, Featurespace, Tink/Salt Edge-class providers) were not surfaced.

Hungarian bank actor names were not yet used systematically as search anchors against vendor sites (MBH Bank, OTP, K&H, Erste Hungary, CIB, Raiffeisen, UniCredit Hungary, Gránit, MagNet, Takarékbank legacy).
Local-language search used 'sajtóközlemény/szállító/szerződés' but not the reference-page vocabulary that actually carries Hungarian vendor wins.
Vendor LinkedIn pages, conference/awards submissions and annual-report customer lists — often the only place a Hungarian win is named — were not covered.
Retail (non-bank) side of the cell is thin — only one POS vendor (GK via Lidl) surfaced; Hungarian retailer self-checkout, payment terminal and loyalty vendor wins remain uncovered.

The HU subsidiaries of global integrators/consultancies (NTT Data Hungary, DXC HU, Accenture HU, IBM HU, Nagarro HU, EPAM HU) were not individually source-mapped in this pass; only their sector context was established.

Subcontracting calls (alvállalkozói felhívás, beszállítói pályázat) issued by integrators themselves — explicitly named in the cell rationale — were only exemplified (Nádor), not systematically enumerated.

State-owned or state-adjacent financial institutions as buyers (Magyar Államkincstár, MNB, Eximbank, MFB, Diákhitel, Takarék/MBH group entities) were not individually checked for their own procurement pages and public-interest data (közadat) publications.
No archival/historical source was identified for pre-EKR (before 2018) Hungarian procurement notices, limiting longitudinal analysis of integrator framework positions.

All URLs in this slice are unverified for liveness; several (t-systems.hu, dorsum.eu, 4ig.hu IR path, kozbeszerzes.hu ertesito path, nisz.hu kozadat path, mnb.hu jelentesek path) were inferred from search snippets or site structure rather than fetched.
EKR and Közbeszerzési Értesítő were identified but their internal search interfaces/APIs were not exercised with the payments keyword set, so no concrete notice inventory exists yet.
Bank acquirers beyond OTP/K&H/MBH/Takarékbank (Erste, Raiffeisen, UniCredit, CIB, Gránit) and independent ISOs/ATM-POS operators were not individually scouted in this pass.

Company-register and contract-transparency sources (e-cegjegyzek/Opten/Bisnode, and central contract-publication obligations under Info tv. §1 melléklet) were not scouted; these can reveal payment-service contracts of state bodies not routed through EKR.
Scheme certification / partner listings (Visa, Mastercard, and terminal vendors such as Ingenico, PAX, Verifone HU partner lists) remain unmapped.
All URLs in this slice are search-result-derived; none were fetched and confirmed reachable in this pass, and several MNB paths appear under both mnb.hu and www.mnb.hu with archive variants.

Deposit/investor-protection and infrastructure-operator registers (OBA, BEVA, GIRO/BKR participant lists, ATM/POS acquirer lists) were not systematically searched in this run, though a BEVA special-database URL was seen on MNB Intézménykereső.
Statistical registers (KSH company demography, TEÁOR-coded business registers) were not covered, which would give sector-level counts of payments-related firms.

The free e-Cégjegyzék service explicitly excludes acquiring all or a significant part of the register, and the beszámoló bulk dataset is sold commercially — the permissible automated collection volume is undefined.

kozadat.hu's central index of üvegzseb disclosures is known to be uneven; many institutions publish contracts only on their own sites, so a central-index-only strategy will under-capture public banking/payments contracts.

Municipality-level contract registers were not enumerated. Hungarian local governments each run their own 'általános közzétételi lista / III.4' page, and municipal account-management and card-acceptance mandates are a core banking market — but this cell only established the generic heading pattern, not a list of the largest municipalities' actual disclosure URLs.

Contract disclosures of state-owned banks and financial vehicles (MFB, Eximbank, Magyar Posta / Posta financial services, Diákhitel Központ, MBH as successor of MKB/Budapest Bank/Takarék) were not individually mapped, although K-Monitor tag pages and a Diákhitel 'Közadatkereső' page were observed.

No audit-institution sources were covered: Állami Számvevőszék (ÁSZ) audit reports on account-management and IT procurement, and Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság (KDB) remedy decisions, both of which expose contested banking/payment tenders in detail.

EU-funded contract archives specific to Hungary (palyazat.gov.hu / Széchenyi támogatott projektek lists, EU Financial Transparency System) were not covered, even though they carry a parallel disclosure duty above the same thresholds and often finance digitalisation and payment infrastructure.

No company-registry source (Opten, Céginfo, e-cegjegyzek / IM Céginformációs Szolgálat) was assessed, so winning-bidder names from award notices cannot yet be resolved to ownership, financials, or group structure.

The specific CPV code set that delimits banking and payments (e.g. 66100000 banking and investment services, 66110000 banking services, 66172000 financial transaction processing, 30144200 / 30123000 ticketing and cash-register machinery, 48xxxxxx financial software) was reasoned about but not verified against actual Hungarian notices.

Hungarian national contract-transparency sources are overwhelmingly Hungarian-only; no English-language mirror of kozadat.hu, EKR or CoRe was found. English coverage exists only at the EU/NGO layer (TED, Opentender, Integrity Watch).
